html:
The Karitiana, who call themselves Yjxa, are a small Indigenous people of Rondônia in the western Amazon of Brazil, south of Porto Velho. They number a few hundred and live by farming, fishing and hunting.

Their language is one of the two surviving Arikém languages, part of the wider Tupian family. Their region was opened up by rubber tappers during the Amazon rubber boom and later by the Madeira Mamoré railway. They are well known in science: their DNA is often used as a reference sample for Native Americans in genetic studies. Blood samples taken from them in 1987 were later sold to laboratories without their consent, a case that caused an outcry in Brazil. Their neighbours include the Paiter Suruí to the southeast.
